newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends up despite greenback strength.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends up despite greenback strength.

text.p: Despite the U.S. dollar's strength in Asia, the Taiwan dollar closed sharply higher on Thursday on current and expected inflows of foreign equity funds for the feverish stock market, dealers said.
The local unit fell to T$27.550 at the open, reflecting the U.S. dollar's firmness against the yen and currencies overseas.
But entries of foreign equity funds, though not in big amount, intensified selling momentum on the greenback, dragging the rate to an intra-day high of T$27.420 in early afternoon.
The rate ended at T$27.444 against Wednesday's T$27.515.
Turnover swelled to an active US$429 million.

Selling from exporters on the U.S. currency emerged after the rate hit an intra-day low of T$27.55 at the opening and strong expectations for foreign fund entries further fuelled the Taiwan dollar's strength.
"There should be more foreign equity funds flowing into the active stock market and such expectations are likely to last for a while," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The rate was expected to move within relatively wide bands in coming sessions with both importers and exporters trading actively, dealers said. A T$27.40-50 trading range was seen.
